Rashi on Chullin 85a:12:1.english: Just as there, [it is] a fit slaughter - as it is written (Genesis 43): "for with me they shall eat":

Rashi on Chullin 85a:14:1.hebrew: ושב הכהן ובא הכהן - בנגעי בתים כתיב, וילפינן מינה גזירה שוה בתורת כהנים: נאמר "ושב הכהן" ונאמר "ובא הכהן" — מה שיבה חולץ וקוצה וטח ונותן לו שבוע, אף ביאה כו'; וכבר פירשתיה יפה בעירובין (בכיצד מעברין) (דף נא.):
Rashi on Chullin 85a:14:1.english: And the priest shall return, and the priest shall come - [This] is written regarding the plagues of houses, and we derive from it a gezerah shavah [verbal analogy] in Torat Kohanim: It is stated, “And the priest shall return,” and it is stated, “And the priest shall come” — just as [with] returning, he removes [the affected stones], scrapes [the walls], replasters, and grants it a week, so too [with] coming, etc.; and I have already explained it thoroughly in Eruvin (in [the chapter] Keitzad Me'abrin) (51a):

Rashi on Chullin 85a:15:1.hebrew: בשחוטי חוץ כתיב (ויקרא יז): "דם שפך":
Rashi on Chullin 85a:15:1.english: Regarding [sacrifices] slaughtered outside [the Temple], it is written (Leviticus 17): "He has shed blood."

Rashi on Chullin 85a:1:1.english: Rather, an uncertain man - and [it] overrides a full Festival:

Rashi on Chullin 85a:2:1.hebrew: ור' יוסי - דלא חשיבא ליה הא פירכא, משום דאזיל לטעמיה דאמר: אפילו אשה ודאית תקעה, ואע"ג דלא מיחייבא; אבל בכסוי, דאילו ידעינן דבהמה היא, ביו"ט אסור לכסות — כוי מספק לא מחללין עליה יו"ט:
Rashi on Chullin 85a:2:1.english: And Rabbi Yosei - [The reason] this refutation is not significant to him is because he follows his [own] reasoning, as he says [that] even a definite woman may blow [the shofar], even though she is not obligated; whereas regarding covering [the blood], where if we knew that it is a domesticated animal it would be forbidden to cover [its blood] on Yom Tov — [for] a koy, out of doubt, we do not desecrate Yom Tov for it:

Rashi on Chullin 85a:3:1.hebrew: סומכות רשות - ואע"ג דלא מיחייבא, ולא אמרינן עבודה עובדת בקדשים. והכא נמי לא אמרינן מחללת יום טוב היא:
Rashi on Chullin 85a:3:1.english: [Women] lay [hands] optionally - even though she is not obligated, and we do not say [that] she is performing labor with consecrated [offerings]. And here too, we do not say [that] she is desecrating the Festival:

Rashi on Chullin 85a:4:1.hebrew: ולמאי דקאמרי רבנן נמי - דאשה אסורה לתקוע, וטומטום דספק הוא דוחה, אית ליה פירכא לתשובה שלהם:
Rashi on Chullin 85a:4:1.english: And even [according] to what the Sages say - that a woman is forbidden to blow [the shofar], yet a tumtum, who is [a case of] uncertainty, overrides [the prohibition] — there is a refutation to their reply:

Rashi on Chullin 85a:4:2.english: What [is distinctive] about the sounding of the shofar, that its definite [obligation] overrides Shabbat in the Temple - Therefore, its uncertain [obligation] overrides a Festival in the provinces [outside the Temple]:

Rashi on Chullin 85a:4:3.english: Can you say [the same] regarding covering [the blood] - [in] that its definite [obligation] does not override Shabbat at all:

Rashi on Chullin 85a:5:1.english: Is it then in effect on other nights - [This is said] as a rhetorical question:

Rashi on Chullin 85a:7:1.english: An undomesticated animal or a bird that [is sentenced to] be stoned - for example, where they were subjected to bestiality, and their verdict was finalized, and [one] slaughtered them:

Rashi on Chullin 85a:7:2.hebrew: וחכמים פוטרין - דשחיטה שאינה ראויה לא שמה שחיטה, ואע"ג דבכסוי "שפיכה" כתיבא, אפילו הכי "אשר יאכל" כתיב. וטעמיה דרבי מאיר מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Chullin 85a:7:2.english: And the Sages exempt [him] - because a slaughter that is not fit [to render the animal permitted for consumption] is not considered "slaughter"; and even though regarding covering [the blood] "pouring" is written [in the verse, rather than "slaughter"], nevertheless "that may be eaten" is written. And Rabbi Meir's reason is explained in the Gemara:

Rashi on Chullin 85a:9:1.english: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] saw [as correct] the statement of Rabbi Meir regarding "it and its offspring" - [namely,] that an unfit slaughter is considered [a valid] slaughter to render him liable.

Rashi on Chullin 85a:9:2.hebrew: ושנאה בלשון חכמים - כדתנן בה (לעיל חולין דף פא:): "רבי שמעון פוטר וחכמים מחייבין", ובכסוי תנן: "ר' מאיר מחייב וחכמים פוטרין". ולקמיה מפרש ואזיל מאי שנא דראה אלו כאן ואלו כאן:
Rashi on Chullin 85a:9:2.english: And he taught it using the term "the Sages" - As we learned in the Mishnah concerning it (above, Chullin 81b): "Rabbi Shimon exempts, and the Sages obligate," and regarding covering [the blood] we learned: "Rabbi Meir obligates, and the Sages exempt." And later on, [the Gemara] proceeds to explain what the difference is [such] that he saw [fit to adopt] these [views] here and those there:

Tosafot on Chullin 85a:13:1.hebrew: דנין שחיטה משחיטה ואין דנין שחיטה מטביחה - הקשה הר"ר נתן: דגבי תשלומי ד' וה' (ב"ק דף עא.) מחייבי רבנן בשחיטה שאינה ראויה, כגון שחט בשבת או לעבודת כוכבים בטובח ע"י אחר, ובשוחט ונמצאת טרפה; והתם הוה ליה למילף טביחה מטביחה, ד"וטבחו" כתיב! וי"ל, דהתם דנין טביחה בעבירה משחיטה דעבירה, ואין דנין טביחה דעבירה מטביחה דהיתר. והכא איצטריך למימר דנין שחיטה משחיטה אפי' אם נמצאת הראשונה טרפה, דהוי שחיטת היתר; אבל אם נמצאת השניה טרפה, שהיא שחיטת עבירה, לא היה צריך לטעמא ד"שחיטה משחיטה". א"נ י"ל, דנין דבר הנאמר בסיני מדבר הנאמר בסיני, ולא מ"טבוח טבח והכן" שלא נאמר בסיני, ואע"ג דהוי טביחה מטביחה; והכא נמי מצי לשנויי הכי, אלא דבלאו הכי משני שפיר. וא"ת: דבריש פ"ב דיבמות (דף יז:) אמרינן דנין אחים מאחים ואין דנין אחים מאחיך, אע"ג דאחים דבני יעקב לא נאמר בסיני? וי"ל, דכיון דילפינן הכא דשמה שחיטה, תו אית לן למימר בכל דוכתי דשמה שחיטה, וליכא למימר דאדרבה נילף טביחה מטביחה התם דלא שמה שחיטה, וכן נאמר בכל דוכתי; דהא כיון דאיכא למימר הכי ואיכא למימר הכי, אית לן למימר דנין דבר הנאמר בסיני מדבר הנאמר בסיני. אבל אי לאו דילפינן הכא שחיטה משחיטה, הוה ילפינן בארבעה וחמשה (ב"ק דף עא.) טביחה מטביחה, אע"ג דלא נאמר בסיני, כדאיתא נמי ביבמות. וא"ת: ור"מ למה ליה למילף משחוטי חוץ? נילף מגופיה, דאותו ואת בנו נוהג בקדשים אע"ג דלאו שחיטה ראויה היא, דהא הוי מחוסר זמן? וי"ל, דניחא ליה למילף משחוטי חוץ, משום דמגופיה איכא למידחי דלא אסר רחמנא אותו ואת בנו בקדשים אלא כשראשון קדשים ושני חולין, דשחיטה ראויה היא:
Tosafot on Chullin 85a:13:1.english: One derives sheḥita from sheḥita, and one does not derive sheḥita from teviḥa - Rabbi Natan raised a difficulty: Regarding the fourfold and fivefold payments (Bava Kamma 71a), the Rabbis obligate [one to pay] for an ineffective slaughter — for example, [if] he slaughtered on Shabbat or for idolatry through another person who slaughtered [for him], or [if] he slaughters and it is found to be a tereifa — and there, [the Gemara] should have derived teviḥa [slaughter] from teviḥa, since "and he slaughtered it" [utvaḥo] is written! And one can answer that there, we derive teviḥa [done] in transgression from sheḥita [done] in transgression, and we do not derive teviḥa [done] in transgression from teviḥa [done] permissibly. And here, it was necessary to say that we derive sheḥita from sheḥita even if the first [animal] was found to be a tereifa, which is a permissible slaughter; whereas if the second [animal] was found to be a tereifa, which is a slaughter [done] in transgression, it would not have needed the reason of "sheḥita from sheḥita." Alternatively, one can answer that we derive something that was stated at Sinai from something that was stated at Sinai, and not from "slaughter an animal [tevo'aḥ tevaḥ] and prepare" (Genesis 43:16), which was not stated at Sinai, even though it is [a case of] teviḥa from teviḥa; and here too, [the Gemara] could have answered thus, except that even without this it answers well. And if you ask: At the beginning of the second chapter of Yevamot (17b), we say that we derive "brothers" from "brothers" and we do not derive "brothers" from "your brother," even though "brothers" [in the story] of the sons of Jacob was not stated at Sinai? And one can answer that once we derive here that it is called sheḥita, we must henceforth say in every place that it is called sheḥita, and one cannot say that, on the contrary, we should derive teviḥa from teviḥa there [to conclude] that it is not called sheḥita and thus say [so] in every place; for since one could say this and one could say that, we must say that we derive something that was stated at Sinai from something that was stated at Sinai. However, if not for the fact that we derive here sheḥita from sheḥita, we would have derived in [the case of] fourfold and fivefold [payments] (Bava Kamma 71a) teviḥa from teviḥa, even though it was not stated at Sinai, just as it is also [derived] in Yevamot. And if you ask: Why does Rabbi Meir need to derive [it] from [the law of] slaughtering consecrated animals outside [the Temple]? Let him derive [it] from [the passage] itself, for [the prohibition of] "it and its young" applies to consecrated animals even though it is not an effective slaughter, since it is premature [meḥusar zeman]? And one can answer that it is preferable for him to derive [it] from [the law of] slaughtering outside [the Temple], because from [the passage] itself one could refute [the derivation by saying] that the Merciful One only prohibited "it and its young" with regard to consecrated animals when the first [animal] is consecrated and the second is non-consecrated, which is an effective slaughter:

Tosafot on Chullin 85a:16:1.hebrew: ואין דנין חולין מקדשים - ומ"מ בקדשים נמי פטר בשחיטה שאינה ראויה, משום דעיקר קרא דאותו ואת בנו בחולין כתיב. ותימה, דבפרק תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף סג.) תנן: רבי שמעון אומר, השוחט פסח בי"ד על החמץ, לשמו חייב, שלא לשמו פטור. ומפרש בקונטרס: משום דהוי פסול, ור"ש לטעמיה דאמר שחיטה שאינה ראויה לא שמה שחיטה. והשתא, התם הוה ליה למילף משחוטי חוץ דשמה שחיטה, דהויא קדשים מקדשים:
Tosafot on Chullin 85a:16:1.english: And one does not derive non-sacred [animals] from consecrated [animals] - Nevertheless, with regard to consecrated [animals] as well, [Rabbi Shimon] exempts [one who performs] an unfit slaughter, because the primary verse of "it and its offspring" is written regarding non-sacred [animals]. And this is astonishing! For in the chapter [entitled] Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 63a) we learned: Rabbi Shimon says, one who slaughters the Paschal offering on the fourteenth [of Nisan] while in possession of leaven — for its own sake, he is liable; not for its own sake, he is exempt. And Rashi explains [that this is] because it is disqualified, and Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning, as he says that an unfit slaughter is not considered slaughter. Now, there he should have derived from [the case of] animals slaughtered outside [the Temple] that it is considered slaughter, since it is [a derivation of] consecrated [animals] from consecrated [animals]:

Tosafot on Chullin 85a:19:1.hebrew: ורבי שמעון אשר יאכל כתיב - אבל אם לא "אשר יאכל", מטביחה לא גמר, משום דלא דמי שפיכה לטביחה כמו שחיטה לטביחה. הקשה הר"ר אליעזר ממי"ץ: אימא דהאי "אשר יאכל" אתא למעוטי אוכל שאין אתה יכול להאכילו לאחרים, כדדריש רבי שמעון "מכל האוכל אשר יאכל" בפרק המנחות והנסכים (מנחות דף קא:) ובפרק העור והרוטב (לקמן חולין דף קכט.), ומרבינן אפילו עוף טמא כיון דמותר בהנאה? וי"ל: דהתם כתיב "מכל האוכל", דמרבה כל אוכל אפילו אסור בהנאה, ואתא "אשר יאכל" למימר שיהא מותר בהנאה; אבל הכא לא כתיב "כל", "אשר יאכל" משמע המותר לישראל לאכול:
Tosafot on Chullin 85a:19:1.english: And Rabbi Shimon [responds]: “That may be eaten” is written - But if not [for the phrase] “that may be eaten,” he would not derive [the exclusion] from “butchering” (tevichah), because “pouring” (shfichah) is not comparable to “butchering” in the way that “slaughter” (shechita) is comparable to “butchering.” Rabbi Eliezer of Metz raised a difficulty: Say that this [phrase] “that may be eaten” comes to exclude food that you cannot feed to others, as Rabbi Shimon expounds [from] “of any food that may be eaten” in the chapter [entitled] HaMenachot veHaNesachim (Menachot 101b) and in the chapter [entitled] HaOr veHaRotev (later, Chullin 129a), and [thus] we would include even a ritually impure bird, since it is permitted for benefit? And one can answer: There, “of any food” is written, which includes all food, even [that which is] forbidden for benefit, and “that may be eaten” comes to say that it must be permitted for benefit; but here, “any” is not written — “that may be eaten” implies that which is permitted for a Jew to eat:

Tosafot on Chullin 85a:3:1.hebrew: נשים סומכות רשות - היינו באקפויי ידא, כדאמר באין דורשין (חגיגה דף טז:), אבל בכל כחה מודה רבי יוסי דאסור; ומייתי הכא: כי היכי דשרי רבי יוסי לסמוך לנשים באקפויי ידא, אע"ג דנראה כעבודה בקדשים, ה"נ תקיעה, דליכא אלא איסורא דרבנן, שרי רבי יוסי בנשים:
Tosafot on Chullin 85a:3:1.english: Women lay [their hands] as an option - This means by resting the hand lightly, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Ein Dorshin (Chagigah 16b), but [leaning] with all her strength, Rabbi Yosei concedes that it is forbidden. And [the Gemara] cites [this] here [to show that] just as Rabbi Yosei permits women to lay [their hands] by resting the hand lightly, even though it appears like performing work with consecrated [animals], so too [regarding] sounding the shofar, where there is only a rabbinic prohibition, Rabbi Yosei permits [it] for women:

Tosafot on Chullin 85a:6:1.hebrew: מה למילה שכן אינה נוהגת בלילות כבימים - ואם תאמר: כיון שאין הפירכא מעין ק"ו שתלוי בדחייה, נשים הפירכא בתוך הק"ו, כמו בכיצד הרגל (ב"ק דף כד:), דבעי למילף שיהא קרן ברשות הניזק משלם נזק שלם משן ורגל, ולא פרכינן "מה לשן ורגל שכן היזקו מצוי" משום שאין הפירכא מעין ק"ו, דהוי מתשלומין? וי"ל, דהתם סברא בעלמא היא; אבל חומרא וקולא דכתיבא, כמו "שאינה נוהגת בלילות כבימים" דהכא, פרכינן אע"ג דלא הוי מעין ק"ו. וכן בפרק קמא דזבחים (דף י.), דיליף שוחט ע"מ לזרוק שלא לשמו פסול מק"ו דשוחט על מנת לזרוק חוץ לזמנו, ופריך: מה לחוץ לזמנו, שכן בכרת:
Tosafot on Chullin 85a:6:1.english: What [is notable] about circumcision, that it does not apply at night as by day - And if you say: since the refutation is not of the same nature as the kal vachomer, which depends on overriding [Shabbat], let us place the refutation inside the kal vachomer — just as in [the chapter entitled] Keitzad HaRegel (Bava Kamma 24b), where [the Gemara] seeks to derive that horn (keren) in the injured party's domain pays full damages from tooth and foot (shen and regel), and we do not refute [it by asking], "What about tooth and foot, whose damage is common?" because the refutation is not of the same nature as the kal vachomer, which deals with payments? One can answer that there it is merely a logical argument; however, [regarding] a stringency or leniency that is explicitly written [in Scripture], such as "it does not apply at night as by day" here, we do refute [with it] even though it is not of the same nature as the kal vachomer. And similarly in the first chapter of Zevachim (10a), where [the Gemara] derives [that] one who slaughters with the intention to sprinkle [the blood] not for its own sake is disqualified from a kal vachomer from one who slaughters with the intention to sprinkle [it] beyond its [allotted] time, and it refutes: What about [intention for] beyond its time, which carries [the penalty of] karet:
